title: [JICA INDONESIA] User Training for Vaccine Icelined Refrigerators in Indonesia February 2023 (Short)
description:
Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA) in collaboration with Bengkulu Provincial Health Office organized the one-day user training on the operation and maintenance of the Vaccine Icelined Refrigerator on 9 February 2023 at Bengkulu City, Bengkulu Province in Indonesia. 
The training was implemented under the JICA’s technical cooperation for “The Project for Strengthening Capacity Building Management of Vaccination and Laboratory for COVID-19 and Other Infectious Diseases".

There were a total of 21 participants, vaccine and cold chain store managers and technicians, from Bengkulu Province, who participated in the training. The training was held in association with the above JICA project to donate 330 units of Vestfrost-made Vaccine Icelined refrigerators (VLS404A) to Indonesia. This user training was composed of lectures and theories and practical “hands-on” sessions to train Cold Chain users to brush up their knowledge and skills on proper maintenance of the equipment and accessories to be supplied by JICA. 

Through this training, we brief this technical support to the Ministry of Health, the Republic of Indonesia officials, and other provincial health office people to urge other target provinces to follow. JICA hope this activity could be widely watched by JICA people and other Japanese who are involved with international cooperation.

title: 【JICA TANZANIA】Changing Farmers’ Mind Set from “Grow and Sell' to ‘Grow to Sell' (TANSHEP) Short ver
description:
Agriculture in Tanzania is an important sector, with about 65% of the population engaged in agriculture and accounting for about 25% of GDP. However, its productivity and profitability were low, and shifting to higher value-added agriculture has been one of the major challenges. One of the reasons for low profitability is that farmers grow and sell crops without knowing the market needs. Therefore, we have been promoting the "SHEP (Smallholder Horticulture Empowerment & Promotion)" , an approach that changes the mindset of farmers from "grow and sell" to "grow to sell," and trying to improve the farming and cultivation skills of horticultural farmers. This video provides an overview of the "SHEP" approach practice in Tanzania and shows success attained by farmers who practice it.

title: Interview "State of Human Security in a Post-pandemic World" with Prof. Mely Caballero-Anthony【JICA】
description:
Professor Mely Caballero-Anthony, Advisor to Human Security and Practices of Empowerment in East Asia research project of JICA Ogata Sadako Research Institute for Peace and Development, provides her insights about the state of Human Security in a post-pandemic world. In the interview, she talks about how the elements of and threats to human security evolve, lessons learned from responses to the pandemic, including remaining gaps, and the concept of empowerment in advancing human security.
For more information on the research project "Human Security and the Practices of Empowerment in East Asia," please check the link below.
https://www.jica.go.jp/jica-ri/research/peace/peace_20191206-20230331.html
 
 【Prof Mely Caballero-Anthony】
Mely Caballero-Anthony is a Professor of International Relations and holds the President's Chair for International Relations and Security Studies.  She is also Head of the Centre for Non-Traditional Security (NTS) Studies at the S. Rajaratnam School of International Studies (RSIS), Nanyang Technological University, Singapore.

00:33 What have been the developments in human security research since its introduction?

05:56 What is the value of exploring the concept of empowerment?

title: Projet « École pour Tous » en Afrique（court）
description:
Projet « École pour Tous » en Afrique : Les données montrent une amélioration spectaculaire de l'éducation des enfants
Les parents du monde entier souhaitent offrir à leurs enfants une éducation de qualité. 
Cependant, en Afrique subsaharienne, par exemple, près de 90 % des enfants d'âge scolaire primaire ne parviennent pas à atteindre les niveaux de compétence minimum en lecture et en mathématiques. 
De plus, la pandémie de COVID-19 a exacerbé la « crise de l'apprentissage » en nécessitant des mesures telles que la fermeture des écoles.
Dans ce contexte, le projet « École pour Tous » de la JICA a considérablement amélioré les compétences académiques de base des enfants africains en améliorant l'environnement d'apprentissage en collaboration avec les écoles, les parents et les communautés locales. 
Le projet, qui a commencé en 2004 dans 23 écoles primaires au Niger, s'est maintenant étendu à environ 70 000 écoles primaires et secondaires dans neuf pays africains, et ses réalisations ont attiré l'attention du monde entier.

Plus de détails peuvent être trouvés dans cet article.
https://www.jica.go.jp/english/news/field/2022/20221118_11.html

title: Supporting Ukraine with made-in-Japan landmine detection technology（Short）
description:
Japanese Technology to Support Demining Efforts in Ukraine! Training on made-in-Japan landmine detection in Cambodia

In January 2023, the Japanese government, through JICA, invited expert officials from the State Emergency Service of Ukraine (SESU) to Cambodia for training on the latest Japanese landmine detectors.

Due to Russian invasion, as much as 30% of the land in Ukraine could be contaminated with hazardous explosive remnants of war, such as landmines and unexploded ordnance. It is estimated that it will take at least 10 years. 

JICA's project aims to remove these explosives in Ukraine as quickly and safely as possible in anticipation of postwar reconstruction.

title: School for All Project（Short）
description:
School for All Project in Africa: Data shows dramatic improvement in children’s education

Parents around the globe want to provide their children with a quality education. 
In Sub-Saharan Africa, for example, almost 90 percent of primary-school-aged children are not achieving the minimum proficiency levels in reading and mathematics. 
Furthermore, the COVID-19 pandemic has exacerbated the “learning crisis” by necessitating such measures as school closures.

Against such a backdrop, the JICA “School for All” project has dramatically improved the basic academic skills of African children by improving the learning environment for children in collaboration with schools, parents, and local communities. 
The project, which started in 2004 at 23 primary schools in Niger, has now spread to about 70,000 primary and secondary schools in nine African countries, and its achievements have attracted worldwide attention.

More details can be found in this article.
https://www.jica.go.jp/english/news/field/2022/20221118_11.html

title: BACK FROM THE RUBBLES-JICA’s cooperation in Nepal-
description: The Gorkha Earthquake in 2015 caused severe loss and damage to heritage monuments in Nepal. JICA dispatched “Cultural Heritage Advisor” to support The Department of Archaeology (DoA) on heritage conservation and to provide technical advice. In Japan, the main concept of the heritage buildings reconstruction is to preserve the authenticity of the building. The Expert, Dr. Toshimichi Okumura has been working for 4 years in Nepal and organized workshops and seminars about cultural heritage buildings rehabilitation for DoA staff and Colleges students. He and DoA are now working on rehabilitation of Shiva Temple with original structure, and using original materials as much as possible as a model of preserving the authenticity.

title: Formation sur la technologie Do-Nou avec la JICA Burkina Faso
description:
Le Burkina Faso est un pays enclavé et sans accès à la mer, la route joue donc un rôle très important dans son développement. Le bureau local de la JICA a offert aux acteurs en charge de l’entretien des routes en terre du pays une formation sur la technologie DO-NOU. Cette technologie développée au Japon est mise en œuvre dans plus de 25 pays en Afrique. 
Grâce à son faible coût et à l’utilisation des matériaux locaux, elle pourrait contribuer à l’entretien de routes en terre aussi bien dans les zones urbaines que rurales. Elle peut aussi être utilisée pour construire des infrastructures de protection tel que des digues, des retenues d’eaux ou des ouvrages de franchissement.

 Энэхүү шинэ тогтолцооны талаар та бүхэнд танилцуулах үүднээс DPUB2 төслөөс нөлөөллийн видеог бэлтгэсэн юм. 2021 оны намраас өвлийг дамжин Токио, Улаанбаатар хотуудад зураг авалт хийж, Токио хотод эвлүүлгийг нь хийсэн 1 минутын энэхүү видеонд дэлгэцийг хоёр хэсэгт хуваан, монголд ажиллаж буй хөгжлийн бэрхшээлтэй ажилтанд япон ажлын байрны дадлагажуулагч зөвлөгөө өгч дадлагажуулж буй байдлыг ойлгомжтойгоор хүргэхийн зэрэгцээ, монгол ажилтнууд инээмсэглэл тодруулан ажиллаж байгааг харуулсан сэтгэл хоногшихуйц видео болсон гэж бодож байна.

title: Good Practice of Employing Persons with Disabilities, Case 1, APU Company, Mongolia
description:
Mongolia Job Coach employment support service awareness-raising video 

　The Ministry of Labour and Social Protection in Mongolia and the JICA technical cooperation Project for Promoting Employment of Persons with Disabilities in Mongolia (DPUB2) train specialist personnel called 'job coach' to match people with disabilities who wish to work with companies. The project is promoting the provision of a 'job coach employment support service' that provides consistent support from job assessment to assignment, adaptation to the workplace and retention.
　To inform people about this new system, which has never existed in Mongolia before, DPUB2 has produced an awareness-raising video, shot in Tokyo and Ulaanbaatar during the autumn and winter of 2021, and edited in Tokyo, the one-minute video splits the screen into two halves, showing persons with disabilities working in Mongolia and a Japanese support. The video is warm and impressive, and symbolically expressing the smiles that are spreading across Mongolia.

title: Words of Sadako Ogata, a Five-Foot Giant
description:

And somehow, she became known as the “Five- Foot Giant”. At times, she would wear a bullet proof vest weighing 15 kilograms. 
What kind of world was she wishing to make? We will look at some of her words, to pass into the future.

description:
JICA marks its 60th anniversary of its cooperation activities with Tanzania in 2022. The activities began in 1962, just one year after the independence of Tanganyika, when a single Government Official was accepted for technical training in Japan. 
Since then, the activities of JICA continued to grow over the years and now include not only technical cooperation and Japan Overseas Cooperation Volunteers (JOCV), but also the provision of grant aid and concessionary loans. Over the 60 years, JICA’s activities have continued to grow and expand to support many social and economic development activities.JICA will carry out its activities in line with Tanzania's development plan.

title: IUJ-JICA Ogata Research Institute Knowledge Forum
description:
Amidst the extensive socioeconomic and political consequences of the COVID-19 pandemic still in effect, the Russian invasion of Ukraine broke out this February. This has created a crisis on top of another crisis, or compounded crises that have put the world into an extremely precarious situation. For example, stagnation of exportation from Russia and Ukraine following the invasion is causing a global supply shortage of food and energy, which is greatly impacting people’s livelihoods in the world. Furthermore, in addition to price surges, significant currency depreciations and worsening national debt situations, the global macroeconomic outlook is worsening as well, as seen in the deceleration of economic growth in China. 
IUJ-JICA Ogata Research Institute Knowledge Forum ‘Security and Development Cooperation in Compounded Crises: the Impacts of the Ukraine Crisis, and State, Economic, and Human Security’ was held on December 16, 2022. The session identified various global challenges under today’s compounded crises from the perspectives of state security, economic security, and human security and then discussed measures to enhance resilience and stability.

title: JICA Volunteers in Saint Lucia - Shiatsu Massage
description:
JICA presents, its Japan Overseas Cooperation Volunteers (JOCV) program in Saint Lucia.

In this series of videos called JICA Volunteers in Saint Lucia, we take a look at the highlights of volunteers` contribution to the socio-development of Saint Lucia. 

Second,we present Mr. Akira TSUNAKAWA. 

As part of a revenue generating initiative by the Saint Lucia Blind Welfare Association (SLBWA), Japan Overseas Cooperation Volunteer (JOCV), Mr. Akira Tsunakawa is teaching shiatsu, (a Japanese massage technique) to blind and visually impaired students. Mr. Tsunakawa, who is totally blind, is a teacher of oriental medicine and has worked with the Yokohama School for the Blind for over 25 years. He is now sharing his vast experience and expertise in shiatsu techniques from his hands to those of his students.

His intentions are to provide the students with shiatsu training to become professional shiatsu therapists. The classes are four times a week from Monday to Thursday and will last for one year. Students are also learning anatomy and physiology as part of the training. The class includes five blind and partially sighted students who have had to wait approximately two years for this valuable opportunity due to the COVID-19 pandemic.

title: Good Practice of Employing Persons with Disabilities, Case 1, APU Company, Mongolia
description:
In Mongolia, legal systems are being developed to guarantee the rights of persons with disabilities (PWDs) and promote their participation in society.What changes will be made to both PWDs and companies when they work in companies? And what considerations are required to further promote the employment of PWDs?
 The Mongolian Ministry of Labour and Social Security and JICA are implementing the Project for Promoting Employment of Persons with Disabilities (DPUB2), in which they are visiting companies that employ PWDs and interviewing PWDs, company personnel, colleagues and sometimes even family members. The articles are part of a series of articles that consider how employment should be for PWDs and companies that bring smiles to the faces of both parties.
 The first video is from the APU Company, the largest beverage manufacturer in Mongolia. Ts. Zhavzmaa, who has a congenital hearing loss and speech impediment, used to lose her confidence because people always pointed out what she couldn't do, such as "I can't hear" or "I can't speak well". However, this has changed dramatically since she started working at the APU Company warehouse a year ago.

title: OGATA Sadako Symposium, "What Would You Do?"
description:
▼ OGATA Sadako Symposium, "What Would You Do?"  ▼

ーWhat we can learn from Ms. OGATA Sadako and how we should live our livesー 


This month marks 3 years since OGATA Sadako, who served as UN High Commissioner for Refugees and President of Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA), passed away in October 2019. The world has changed dramatically in just 3 years.


"What would you do?" If Ms. Ogata were alive, she might say this.


On November 15, 2022, JICA held a symposium to discuss the future of the world and Japan by reflecting on OGATA's life and achievements.


Approximately 4,200 people attended the symposium, and we hope that the audience was able to learn Ms. OGATA's way of life and way of thinking, and that it provided an opportunity for each of us, who have been entrusted with her baton, to think about how we should live our lives.


▼Program
00:03:51 1. Video message: Mr. Filippo Grandi, UN High Commissioner for Refugees
00:08:12 2. Keynote Speech: Ms. NAKAMITSU Izumi, UN Under-Secretary-General and High Representative for Disarmament Affairs
00:18:31 3. Short movie: "Words of OGATA　Sadako, a diminutive giant"
00:29:32 4. Panel Discussion　
What would you do? -What would you learn from OGATA Sadako and how would you live your life?
Moderator: Ms. DODEN Aiko  (NHK World Newsline InDepth anchor)
Panelists (in order of program)

title: JJ Partnership
description:
"JJ Partnership" has finally been released, following "Reggae Bon Bon" as one of songs of The Reggae Bon Bon Project.

0n 17th September, 2022 it was held "Jamaica 60: New Frontier of JJ Partnership," an official event to commemorate the 60th independence anniversary of Jamaica, which was organized by JICA and the Embassy of Jamaica in Japan. On this occasion this content as unveiled to the world for the first time. The content　was created as JICA's original official content for the 60th independence anniversary of Jamaica in 2022, the Japan-Caribbean friendship year in 2024, and the 60th diplomatic anniversary between Japan and Jamaica.

The "Reggae Bon Bon Project" was born from the conversation between Ambassador Richards and the JICA Latin America and the Caribbean Department, and many people has been expressed sympathy for this union of band and Bon dance. 

Reggae music, which was registered as a UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage in 2018, was to be an important content for Jamaica's cultural transmission and international exchange during the events commemorating 60th independence anniversary of Jamaica. 
On the other hand, while the COVID-19 didn’t allow the desired transmission of information, based on the successful experience of "Bon for Africa - Bon Dance in Africa", which JICA implemented as a TICAD PR project in 2019 with Mr. Ukon Takafuji and others, the idea of "Reggae Bon Dance" was born and the project was launched in the spring of 2022.

The Reggae Bon dance was completed by Mr. Eiji Tani who has worked with numerous professional artists, Mr. Ukon Takafuji who served as the executive committee chairperson, Mr. Makarafin who is a inheritor of roots reggae and has been working as a professional artist in a wide areas and genres, Mr. Rikiya Nakagawa who is a skilled guitarist that has toured around the world withhis own band, and Mr. ANSA who is a soulful reggae vocalist based in Yokohama. The "Reggae Bon Dance",a fusion of reggae and Bon dance, is expected to become a project that will color various scenes of development and exchange between the two countries in the future.

Composition: Kota Sakaguchi

title: JICA Indonesia organized 2 days maintenance training on Cold Chain equipment in Sept 2022 (Full)
description:
Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA) in collaboration with West Java Provincial Health Office organized the 2 days training of the maintenance of Cold Chain equipment on 13 and 14 September at Bandung, West Java. The training was implemented under the JICA’s technical cooperation for“The Project for Strengthening Capacity Building Management of Vaccination and Laboratory for COVID-19 and Other Infectious Disease".

There were total of 14 participants, vaccine and cold chain technicians, from 7 areas such as South Sulawesi, West Java, West Kalimantan participated in the training. The training was held in association with the above JICA project to donate 330 units of Vestfrost made Vaccine Icelined refrigerators to Indonesia. The items which are under procurement through UNICEF also include voltage stabilizers, temperature data loggers and spare part kits. The units will arrive at Jakarta in December 2022 and will then transported to the target 22 provinces to strengthen Cold Chain infrastructure to store COVID-19 vaccines and routine childhood vaccines. 

This training was composed with the lectures and theories and practical“hand-on" sessions to train trainers to brush up their knowledge and skills on proper maintenance of the equipment and accessories to be supplied by JICA. Through this training, we brief this technical support to the central Ministry of Health officials and other provincial health office people to urge other target provinces to follow. JICA hope this activity could be widely watched by JICA people and other Japanese who are involved with international cooperation. JICA appreciates all participants for their active participation for the training!

title: Floricultura Argentina(avance)
description:
En la historia de la inmigración japonesa a la Argentina es ampliamente conocido, que muchos de los inmigrantes japoneses se dedicaron a la floricultura. 
　En la década del '70 JICA estableció el Centro Tecnológico de Flori-Fruti-Horticultura (conocido como CETTEFHO) como parte de su apoyo a los inmigrantes. Más tarde, con la plena integración de la comunidad de japoneses y sus descendientes, el centro tecnológico modificó sus funciones y fue transferido al Instituto Nacional de Tecnología Agropecuaria (INTA) en 2004, donde renació como el actual Instituto de Floricultura.
　El Instituto de Floricultura del INTA se ha desarrollado hasta convertirse en un líder de la investigación florícola no sólo en el país sino también en la región. En la actualidad, el sistema de investigación se ha ampliado enormemente, se han introducido diversas variedades nuevas mediante la mejora y el desarrollo, y se ha establecido una red en torno al instituto para proporcionar orientación técnica a los floricultures de todo el país. Además, en los últimos años, en colaboración con empresas japonesas, el instituto ha establecido un sistema por el cual los beneficios o regalías se distribuyen también a los lugares de recolección de recursos genéticos utilizados en el desarrollo de nuevas variedades.
  JICA en conjunto con el gobierno argentino, impulsa la cooperación triangular con el INTA y en los últimos 10 años ha implementado el programa de capacitación para terceros países en la región de  América Latina y el Caribe.
  Este vídeo muestra la contribución de los inmigrantes y de los nikkei en el área de la floricultura en Argentina, la cooperación por parte de JICA, y el papel que desempeña el INTA en el desarrollo de esta industria en el país.

title: Project History Launch “Japan-Thailand Environmental Cooperation -35 Years of People-to-People Ties”
description:
JICA Ogata Research Institute has published the "Project History" book series, which looks back on JICA's projects, analyzing and summarizing their trajectories and achievements. As the 29th volume in this series, "Japan-Thailand Environmental Cooperation: 35 Years of People-to-People Ties" has been published. 

This book introduces the history of Japan-Thailand environmental cooperation, focusing on people-to-people ties and summarizing the growth of both the Japanese and Thai parties involved. Fukuda, Seki and Watanabe, three former JICA experts who wrote the book, emphasize that "it is the relationship of trust between people that determines the success or failure of a project. The humanistic activities of these "old generation experts," who do not fit into the framework of project evaluation, provide us with a great deal of insight into the nature of development cooperation.

On May 31, 2022, a seminar was held to commemorate the publication of the book. After an introduction of the book by a representative of the book's author group, a panel discussion by various stakeholders and a roundtable discussion with young experts was held on the theme of building, maintaining, and passing on trust in international cooperation.

title: Side Event COSP-15 The Revolution of Independent Living in Latin America
description:
Side Event｜15th Session of the Conference of States Parties to the CRPD 15 June 2022 (18:00-19:15) Independent Living Revolution in Latin America: Persons with Disabilities as Protagonists of International Cooperation

The session explores how the independent living movement has been advancing in Latin America with the initiative of persons with disabilities, supported by their peers within the region and beyond. It looks at how international cooperation has facilitated an awareness of persons with disabilities of their right to independent living, the establishment of the first independent living center in Costa Rica, and the creation of the Latin American Network for Independent Living (RELAVIN).
The discussion focuses on the experiences of the RELAVIN members at different stages of their journey on independent living. It ensures the effectiveness of international cooperation delivered by organizations of persons with disabilities and the critical role of development agencies. The session makes a call to action to all stakeholders including organizations of persons with disabilities to collaborate for the development of policies and systems for independent living.

title: Evento Paralelo COSP-15 Revolución de la Vida Independiente en Latino América
description:
Evento paralelo de la 15°Conferencia de los Estados Partes en la Convención sobre los Derechos de las Personas con Discapacidad “Revolución de la Vida Independiente en Latino América: Personas con Discapacidad como Protagonistas de la Cooperación Internacional” 
 
La sesión explorará cómo el movimiento de vida independiente ha ido avanzando en América Latina con la iniciativa de las personas con discapacidad, apoyadas por sus pares dentro y de japón. Se analizará cómo la cooperación internacional ha facilitado la concienciación de las personas con discapacidad sobre su derecho a la vida independiente, el establecimiento del primer centro de vida independiente en Costa Rica y la creación de la Red Latinoamericana de Vida Independiente (RELAVIN).

El diálogo se centra en las experiencias de los miembros de RELAVIN en las diferentes etapas de su camino hacia la vida independiente. Al compartir sus experiencias, la sesión pretende demostrar cómo la cooperación internacional puede facilitar el movimiento de la vida independiente y hace un llamamiento a la acción a todas las partes interesadas, incluidas las organizaciones de personas con discapacidad, para que colaboren en el desarrollo de políticas y sistemas de vida independiente

title: Responsive learning initiative taken for Out-of-School Children in Pakistan
description:
There are 22.8 million out-of-school children and youth (OOSC) in Pakistan. Out of the number, 78% are overage, in other words, missed chance to enroll formal education system at appropriate age. 

Hassnain, 12 years boy who had never been to school and working in a riksha workshop in Multan, South Punjab, was one of them. 

The Advancing Quality Alternative Learning Project (AQAL) Phase 2 is working with the Government of Pakistan to provide quality responsive education through Accelerated Learning Program (ALP) for OOSC. Morning school for working children in which Hassnain studies, is one of the ALP school established by the government. Upon completion of the ALP, he will obtain certificate and it is officially recognized equivalent to formal education completion.

Hassnain dreams to be happier with his family and be a person to contribute to his society. ALP supports him to make his dream come true by providing flexible learning opportunities.

title: 【Water×IoT】Innovation for Rural Water Supply in Africa【DMS + SUNDA】
description:
Uganda's rural communities have been suffering from frequent breakdown of boreholes, due to lack of budget and capacity for proper operation and maintenance (O & M).

To solve these challenges, new innovative approaches are developed; "DMS" and "SUNDA".

"DMS" (Direct Management System) is a system in which an independent expertized organization provides timely and professional O & M of hand pump facilities in rural areas. 

"SUNDA" is an IoT "pay-as-you-fetch" prepaid system for hand pumps, which physically and psychologically enables fair contribution collection.

Result of the pilot project by Ministry of Water and Environment, Uganda and JICA collaboration with SUNDA Technology Global, 
 the amount of contribution collected DOUBLED
 caretakers free from heavy duties of money collection 
 users enjoy fairness, transparency and accountability of collected money

By covering 300 boreholes, DMS+SUNDA becomes financially self-sustaining. DMS+SUNDA can breakthrough structural challenges of rural water supply in developing countries.

Avant la TICAD8, l'Agence japonaise de coopération internationale (JICA), en collaboration avec les représentants de ses principales agences partenaires, organise cet événement de haut niveau pour discuter des moyens de faire progresser la coopération au développement en Afrique face aux crises actuelles.

title: High-level Symposium: Rethinking Development Cooperation with Africa in Light of Global Crises
description: The 8th Tokyo International Conference on African Development (TICAD8), to be held this August, is expected to be an opportunity to showcase strong international solidarity to overcome Africa’s challenges. Ahead of TICAD8, the Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA) is hosting this high-level event to discuss paths for advancing development cooperation in Africa in response to the current crises with representatives of its important partner agencies.

title: Study in Japan with JICA Development Studies Program!!
description:
JICA Development Studies Program (JICA-DSP) invites future leaders from partner countries to Japan and offers them the opportunity to learn about Japan’s modernization and development experience which differs from those of Europe and the U.S., and its wisdom as a country that provided cooperation toward the progress of developing countries after World War II. JICA-DSP is co-organized by various universities in Japan and JICA. Through those program, JICA hope that participants will gain a deep understanding of Japan, so that they may use this knowledge to contribute to the development of home countries. （Produced in March 2022）

title: Seminar "World Development Report 2022: Finance for an Equitable Recovery"
description:
World Bank Group and JICA Ogata Research Institute hosted a seminar "World Development Report 2022: Finance for an Equitable Recovery" on May 11, 2022. 

At this seminar, Leora Klapper, WDR 2022 Director, Mahesh Uttamchandani, the Practice Manager for Financial Inclusion & Infrastructure in the Finance, Competitiveness, and Innovation Global Practice at the World Bank Group, and Beniamino Savonitto, an Economist in the Sector Economics and Development Impact department of the International Finance Corporation explained the main findings of the report. Yoshino Naoyuki, Professor Emeritus, Keio University, and Harada Tetsuya, Senior Executive Research Fellow, JICA Ogata Research Institute shared comments.

title: 【JICA with Bangladesh: Reaching 50th Year and Way Forward】Panel Discussion
description:
Soon after the independence of Bangladesh in 1971, Japan was one of the first countries to establish diplomatic relations on 10 February 1972. To commemorate the 50th Anniversary of that occasion, grand celebrations were held both in Dhaka and Tokyo. The collaborative relationship between Bangladesh and Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA) began in 1973 with the dispatching of Japan Overseas Cooperation Volunteers. In the context of this milestone year, the Embassy of Bangladesh in Japan, in collaboration with JICA, is holding the seminar to look back on the cooperation with JICA so far and to explore ways to further strengthen the partnership in the future. The seminar held on Friday, 10 June 2022.
This is Panel Discussion by Mr. Syed Nasir ERSHAD, Economic Minister, Bangladesh Embassy of Tokyo.

title: Knowledge forum: International student mobility and higher education during COVID-19
description:
The coronavirus pandemic (COVID-19) has left no corner of our lives untouched, with higher education as no exception. As of April 2020, approximately 220 million tertiary students worldwide faced disruption to their education as universities temporarily closed due to the pandemic. Since then, as an emergency measure, classes have been widely held online in Japan and globally. Moreover, restrictions on international travel have greatly impacted students with plans to study abroad, forcing them to postpone or cancel their plans or change thei r study locations.

JICA Ogata Research Institute Knowledge Forum “International Student Mobility and Higher Education in the age of COVID-19: Reflections from Oxford University and the University of Tokyo” was held on January 18, 2022. Professor Kariya Takehiko of Oxford University and Professor Takahara Akio of the University of Tokyo discussed the current situation and challenges facing education at th ese two universities in the context of the COVID-19 pandemic. They shared their visions for study abroad programs and university education both during the pandemic and in the post-COVID world.

title: Knowledge Forum: Diffusion of the Japanese Rice Farming Technologies to Asia a nd further to Africa
description:
At this Knowledge Forum which was held March 22, 2022, Kobe University Professor Otsuka Keijiro, who has spent many years conducting research on development issues, focusing on agriculture in Asia and Africa, gave a lecture on the history of the transfer of rice farming technologies from Japan to Asia, and the possibility of the rice Green Revolution in Africa. We had an in-depth discussion with Otsuka regarding the major questions of what is important for bringing about the rice Green Revolution in Africa, and how JICA should support that. Note that Otsuka gave a lecture with the same title as this forum at the Imperial New Year's Lectures in January, 2022.

title: AUDA-NEPAD and JICA Ogata Research Institute Joint Book Launch Webinar (Session 1)
description:
JICA Ogata Research Institute and Africa Union Development Agency (AUDA-NEPAD) Policy Bridge Tank jointly organized two book launch webinars on the theme of industrial development.

Session 1 of the webinar series shared the research findings from the book “Policy Learning for Industrial Development and the Role of Development Cooperation.” This volume contemplates Japanese development experiences that developi ng country’s policy makers can refer to when forming and implementing industr ial policies. The book also introduces development policy support, a type of J apanese intellectual cooperation aimed at providing hands-on policy advice and  promoting the learning process of partner countries through joint work. In th is webinar, authors of the book chapters presented their work and exchanged th oughts with AUDA-NEPAD discussants.

title: AUDA-NEPAD and JICA Ogata Research Institute Joint Book Launch Webinar (Session 2)
description:
JICA Ogata Research Institute and Africa Union Development Agency (AUDA-NEPAD)  Policy Bridge Tank jointly organized two book launch webinars on the theme of  industrial development.

Session 2 of the webinar series shared the research findings from the book “Promoting Quality and Productivity Improvement/ Kaizen in Africa.” JICA began implementing various Kaizen projects in Africa since 2006. It has recently sta rted promoting the Africa Kaizen Initiative (AKI) in collaboration with the Af rican Union Development Agency - the New Partnership for Africa’s Development
 (AUDA-NEPAD) and the Pan-Africa Productivity Association (PAPA). This volume addresses how development cooperation to promote Kaizen can effectively suppor t the process of “translative adaptation” by partner countries. In this webinar, authors of the book chapters presented their work and exchanged thoughts with African discussants.

title: ”Хүүхдийн хөгжил - Бүгдийн оролцоо”
description:
ЖАЙКА олон улсын хамтын ажиллагааны байгууллага, Боловсрол, шинжлэх ухааны яам, Хөдөлмөр, нийгмийн хамгааллын яам хамтран 2020-2024 онд “Тусгай хэрэгцээт боловсрол шаардлагатай хүүхдэд үзүүлэх эрүүл мэнд, боловсрол, нийгмийн хамгааллын үйлчилгээг сайжруулах төсөл”-ийн 2-р шатыг хэрэгжүүлэн хөгжлийн хоцрогдол, зан үйлийн асуудалтай хүүхдийн хөгжлийг дэмжиж мөн нийгмийн тэгш оролцоог хангахад дэмжлэг үзүүлэн ажиллаж байна.  
Жил бүрийн 6 дугаар сарын 1-ний  “Хүүхдийн эрхийг хамгаалах өдөр”-ийг тохиолдуулан тус төслийн түгээн дэлгэрүүлэх зорилтот сургууль буюу нийслэлийн 149-р сургуулийн сурагч M. Тамирболдын тухай мэдээллийг та бүхэндээ хүргүүлж байна. (Зөвхөн монгол хэлээр)

title: Farmers' Voices - Interviews with farmers who participated in SHEP training (JICA SENEGAL)
description:
Smallholder Horticulture Empowerment & Promotion (SHEP) Approach have developed in Kenya through technical cooperation project by JICA which started from 2006 and succeeded in increasing farmers' income.  It aims to improve farmers' income by changing their mindset from "grow and sell" to "grow to sell" and improving their farming and cultivation skills.
This video is an interview with farmers who participated in the Market Survey, Stakeholder forum, Family budgeting, and Demand-driven technical training, which are part of the SHEP approach training.

title: Voix d'agriculteurs - Interviews d'agriculteurs ayant participé à la formation SHEP (JICA SENEGAL)
description:
L'approche SHEP (Smallholder Horticulture Empowerment & Promotion) s'est développée au Kenya en 2006 grâce à un projet de coopération technique de la JICA et a permis d'augmenter les revenus des agriculteurs.  L’approche SHEP vise à améliorer les revenus des agriculteurs en changeant leur mentalité de "produire et vendre" à "produire pour vendre" et en améliorant leurs compétences agricoles et culturales.
Cette vidéo est une interview d'agriculteurs ayant participé à l'étude de marché, au forum de rencontre, à la caisse familiale et à la formation technique axée sur la demande, qui font partie de la formation de l'approche SHEP.

title: JICA Chair Special Lecture ‘Japan after World War II and Japan-China Relations in the Modern Era’
description: In order to expand the opportunities of Japanese studies in developing countries, JICA launched the “JICA Chair (JICA Program for Japanese studies)” in collaboration with leading universities in partner countries. On March 22, 2022, the opening ceremony for JICA Chair program was held at the University of Belgrade, Serbia. More than 100 participants, mainly the students of the Faculty of Philology at the University, attended. After the ceremony, Prof. Akio Takahara, the executive director of JICA Ogata Research Institute, delivered a special lecture on how Japan's foreign policy and Japan-China relations have changed since the end of World War II and the Cold War.

title: 【SHEP】Autonomization and Professionalization of Small Farmers:The case of Madagascar
description:
In Madagascar, the SHEP Approach is used for the education of young rural entrepreneurs. As they gain awareness through market survey and record keeping, they become able to develop strategies for their farm management and apply SHEP to various agricultural products.
Smallholder Horticulture Empowerment & Promotion (SHEP) Approach have developed in Kenya through technical cooperation project by JICA which started from 2006 and succeeded in increasing farmers' income.  It aims to improve farmers' income by changing their mindset from "grow and sell" to "grow to sell" and improving their farming and cultivation skills.

title: School for All « The Challenges that create the future » [PUPIL VERSION]
description:
The Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA) in Niger has been implementing the "School for All" project since 2004 to improve the quality of basic education through collaboration with the Ministry of National Education, the school and the community through the School Management Committees (SMC) in primary and secondary schools.

Within the framework of the project "School for All: Project for Improvement in Basic Education Quality and Girl-Boy Parity through School-Community Collaboration", JICA has produced 3 documentary films whose main actors are: the members of the SMC, the teacher and the pupil at the basic education level, and each in the regions of Zinder, Maradi and Tahoua with the title "The Challenges that create the future".

This pupil version focuses on the impact of the project activities on the improvement of learners' learning.

We, through these 3 documentary films, would like to bring the audience to experience the impacts of the activities of the School For All project in Niger in collaboration with the Ministry of Education, within the framework of improving education in Niger.

title: Ecole Pour Tous « Les challenges qui créent le futur » [VERSION ELEVE]
description:
L’Agence Japonaise de Coopération Internationale (JICA) au Niger met en œuvre depuis 2004 le Projet « Ecole Pour Tous » afin d’améliorer entre autres la qualité au niveau de l'éducation de base grâce à la collaboration avec le Ministère de l’Education Nationale, l’école et la communauté à travers les Comités de Gestion Décentralisée des Etablissements Scolaires/Comités de Gestion des Etablissements Scolaires au Secondaire (CGDES/COGES-ES).

Dans le cadre du Projet « Ecole Pour Tous : Projet d’Amélioration de la Qualité et de la Parité Filles-Garçons au Niveau de l’Education de Base à travers la Collaboration Ecole-Communauté », la JICA a produit 3 films documentaires dont les principaux acteurs sont: les membres du COGES, l’enseignant et l’élève au niveau de l’éducation de base, et chacun dans les régions de Zinder, Maradi et Tahoua avec comme titre " Les challenges qui créent le futur".

Cette version de l’élève, c’est pour mettre l’accent sur l’impact des activités du Projet sur l’amélioration de l’apprentissage des apprenants.

La JICA, à travers ces 3 films documentaires, souhaiterait amener les spectateurs à vivre les impacts des activités du projet Ecole Pour Tous au Niger en collaboration avec le Ministère de l’Education Nationale, dans le cadre de l’amélioration de l’éducation au Niger.

title: Indonesia-Japan Collabonations - MRT "Restoring Hope for the Cities"
description: MRT Jakarta Phase 1's project, from Lebak Bulus to Bundaran HI stretches for 15.7 km, was built with funding from Japan through ODA loan program, with the assistance of JICA. MRT Jakarta is the first underground train In Indonesia, which its operation started in March 2019. Constructed in the heart and capital of Indonesia, Jakarta, this project was initiated to solve the problem of traffic congestion, and also expected to improve the people's quality of life, able to move the wheels of the economy, and restore dreams for the residents of this city.

title: Indonesia-Japan Collabonations - Patimban Port "Connecting Economical Veins"
description: Patimban Port is a collaboration project between the Government of Japan and Indonesia through JICA. Build on a land of 654 acres in Subang, West Java, Patimban Port is currently one of the largest port in Indonesia. This port, connected to the toll road and several priority industrial areas, such as Bekasi, Karawang, and Purwakarta is expected to become one of the veins in world trading, and to be the key link between industry, as well as supporting acceleration of export-import sector.

title: Indonesia-Japan Collabonations - Transportation Sector "Building the Future"
description: The collaboration between JICA and Indonesia has been going for more than 60 years, with supports on Indonesia's development in various fields, including the transportation and logistic sector. JICA takes part in accelerating various mega tranportation and logistic projects in Indonesia, including the construction of MRT Jakarta, Patimban Port, the development of several international airports such as Ngurah Rai Airport in Bali and Juanda Airport in Surabaya, and also the construction and expansion of Merak-Bakaheuni Ferry Terminal.

title: 【JICA DX】Concept Movie
description:
This is a movie on JICA’s partnership approach on digital development. It shows the case of Melody International Ltd., a Japanese health-tech start-up company working on maternal and child health. The product "Melody i" is a cloud-type mobile fetal monitor and perinatal e-Health platform that allows doctors to view data and communicate their diagnosis with pregnant women from distance.
In JICA’s global agenda for Digital for Development, we are seeking innovative solutions and technologies to add values that can be combined with our tested conventional methods.  We welcome collaboration with other partners to achieve our goal, "digital transformation to improve well-being for all."

title: 【JICA DX】Partner Interview (Melody International Ltd.)
description: To contribute to digital development in JICA's partner countries, it is essential to collaborate with partner organizations/companies with advanced technologies and innovative ideas. This video introduces an example of JICA's approach for digital for development along with an interview story of Melody International Ltd, an Japanese start-up that works on maternal and child health issues in Thailand and Bhutan. JICA works for digital development by co-creation with various partners.

title: 【JICA-PRESSMN】La mise en œuvre des soins de maternité et de néonatal respectueux
description:
C’est le résumé d’un film documentaire à travers des témoignages d'acteurs de santé sénégalais, l’historique et les expériences de la coopération entre le Japon et le Sénégal en mise en pratique des soins respectueux dans le cadre du PRESSMN (Projet de Renforcement des Soins de Santé Maternelle et Néonatale). 

Le Ministère de la Santé et de l'Action Sociale, en partenariat avec la JICA, a créé le PRESSMN en 2009. Depuis, le PRESSMN poursuit ses efforts pour améliorer la qualité des soins et la disponibilité des services de santé maternelle et néonatale afin de contribuer à la réduction du taux de mortalité maternelle et néonatale au Sénégal. 

La version complète est aussi disponible sur cette chaine.

title: 【JICA-PRESSMN】La mise en œuvre des soins de maternité et de néonatal respectueux  (version complète)
description:
Ce film documentaire raconte, à travers les témoignages d'acteurs de santé sénégalais, l’historique et les expériences de la coopération entre le Japon et le Sénégal, en mise en pratique des soins respectueux dans le cadre du PRESSMN (Projet de Renforcement des Soins de Santé Maternelle et Néonatale). 

Le Ministère de la Santé et de l'Action Sociale du Sénégal, en partenariat avec la JICA, a créé le PRESSMN en 2009. Depuis, le projet poursuit ses efforts pour améliorer la qualité des soins et la disponibilité des services de santé maternelle et néonatale afin de contribuer à la réduction du taux de mortalité maternelle et néonatale au Sénégal.

title: 【JICA Project NINJA】Cytex Technologies
description:
Cytex Technologies is one of the 5 winners of the NINJA, while 110 companies applied to the project. The company produces VTM test kits for the PCR test, obtaining CE certification. 
In reality,  small laboratories cannot import thousands of VTM at one time from abroad. In this concern, the VTM kit will be packaged in a pack of 50 per Box. Further, laboratories in other countries in the Southern African region (SADC countries) may face the same situation, indicating that the market can be expanded from  Botswana to Angola,  Namibia,  Zambia, and  Zimbabwe. By taking a survey, the needs of a small lot of VTMs will be assessed.

title: 【JICA Project NINJA】IoT Technologies
description:
IoT Communications is one of the 5 winners of the NINJA, while 110 companies applied for the project. 
The company introduced a  Low  Power  Wide  Area  Network  (LPWAN)  service for the first time,  to support an application that employs ‘smart wristbands’ to monitor the safety status and geographical whereabouts of people with a need for protective surveillance. LPWAN service will be expanded in Botswana by the company, and their contribution will open up another potential for future life in Botswana.

title: A Century of Education Study in Japan: Student Exchange Program Video
description:
Japan has been providing Official Development Assistance (ODA) programs in several sectors in Nepal to support its development. It has helped foster human resources, technology transfer and infrastructure development through various technical cooperation projects.
As part of its cooperation in the capacity-building segment, Japan supports in dispatching Nepalese students to Japan for further education courses such as masters, doctorate, etc. So far, many Nepalese students have undertaked this program, pursued degrees in carious fields, and have benefitted immensely. In the year 2022, Nepal is celebrating 120th aniversaty since the first Nepalese students were dispatched to Japan.

title: A story of Friendship and Assistance
description:
A Story of Friendship and Assitance

This short animated film is the story of a girl named Areeba Saleha, born to a family hailing from Abbottabad, Pakistan. Her lifelong friendship with JICA started with her birth at the Children's Hospital in Islamabad. Areeba's parents raised her through thick and thin, but JICA's assistance in health, disaster management, education, and water and sanitation, at every step of the way, did befriend her. Today, Areeba has set up her own fashion apparel brand and is a role model for many children like her who deserve a good life. Her story embodies JICA's vision and mission of decades of partnership with the people of Pakistan.

title: COVID-19 Webinar Series #10 “Building Health Systems toward Resilient UHC with/after the Pandemic”
description:
In order to respond to the COVID-19 pandemic and sustain other health services, countries have been required to rapidly increase and reorganize health service delivery capacity, such as availability of hospital beds, allocation of health human resource and so on. Some countries may have had a legal framework or policy tool to enable such rapid increase, and others may have taken other approaches to deliver the services efficiently and equitably under the resource limited situation, such as remote services. However, it has not been sufficiently clear how countries took actions.

In the 10th JICA COVID-19 Webinar, we listened to different countries’ experience and lessons of preparedness and adaption of health service delivery to cope with COVID-19 and other health needs, and discussed what implications this experience has for the efforts to achieve resilient UHC with and after the Pandemic.

title: Digital Transformation for empowering rural women in Pakistan (long)
description:
This video introduces digital transformation brought about for women in rural area in Pakistan. 

In rural areas of Pakistan, just one in ten internet users are women. Much needs to be done to bridge this digtal devide. Light-F project implemented by JICA and the Women Development Department of Sindh Government, in collaboration with Sindh Rural Support Organization (SRSO) launched an on-line digital marketing training program using smartphone. The goals included income generation and capacity development of women from 20 villages in rural Sindh's Sukkur area. You will witness the power of digital tools to change life and open the doors for opportunities for women in rural areas.

title: Do you want to know more about the ESMATE Project? (JICA EL SALVADOR)

title: ¿Quieres conocer más sobre el Proyecto ESMATE? (VIDEO 5 / JICA EL SALVADOR)
description:
A continuación puedes ver el video completo para conocer más sobre qué es ESMATE(Proyecto de Mejoramiento de los Aprendizajes de Matemática en Educación Básica y Educación Media), ejecutado entre JICA y el Ministerio de Educación de El Salvador. 
Como se crearon los materiales educativos ESMATE, quienes participan y como funcionaron durante la pandemia de COVID-19.

title: Proyecto ESMATE y la pandemia de COVID-19 (VIDEO 4 / JICA EL SALVADOR)
description: En 2020, a pesar que “Proyecto ESMATE” había terminado en junio de 2019, el Ministerio de Educación de El Salvador continuó actualizando, imprimiendo y distribuyendo los materiales educativos de ESMATE, lo que permitió facilitar el proceso de transición de clases presenciales a clases virtuales asegurando la continuidad de la enseñanza de los niños y niñas salvadoreños. En este video, que la cuarta y última parte de los videos especialmente elaborados para darte a conocer más sobre ESMATE, te presentamos los usos y ventajas que tuvieron los materiales ESMATE durante la pandemia de COVID-19 gracias al liderazgo y visión del Ministerio de Educación de El Salvador.

title: Proyecto ESMATE, más que solo materiales educativos (VIDEO 3 / JICA EL SALVADOR)
description: La elaboración y actualización de los materiales educativos producidos por el “Proyecto de Mejoramiento de los Aprendizajes de Matemática en Educación Básica y Educación Media - ESMATE” han implicado desde el inicio en 2015, todo un proceso de seguimiento y evaluación en el cual participan docentes, directores, técnicos entre otros. En esta tercera entrega de cuatro videos especialmente elaborados para darte a conocer más sobre ESMATE, te presentamos el proceso técnico detrás del uso de los materiales educativos de ESMATE.

title: Proyecto ESMATE y sus materiales educativos (VIDEO 2 / JICA EL SALVADOR)
description: El “Proyecto de Mejoramiento de los Aprendizajes de Matemática en Educación Básica y Educación Media”, mejor conocido como “Proyecto ESMATE”, entre 2015 y 2019, elaboró 3 materiales educativos principales: Libros de texto, cuadernos de ejercicios y guías metodológica de primer grado a bachillerato. Para conocer más, sobre el proceso de elaboración y el uso de cada material educativo, te presentamos el segundo video de cuadro especialmente elaborados para darte a conocer más sobre ESMATE y su continuidad a la fecha. Continua pendiente de nuestras siguientes publicaciones para seguir viendo más.

title: Proyecto ESMATE, un esfuerzo que inició en 2015 (VIDEO 1 / JICA EL SALVADOR)
description: En 2015, junto con el Ministerio de Educación de El Salvador, iniciamos la ejecución del “Proyecto de Mejoramiento de los Aprendizajes de Matemática en Educación Básica y Educación Media”, mejor conocido como “Proyecto ESMATE”. Aunque el proyecto finalizó en junio de 2019, sus resultados siguen trascendiendo en la educación de los niños y niñas salvadoreños. Este día, la oficina de JICA lanza la presentación de 1 de 4 videos especialmente elaborados para darte a conocer más sobre ESMATE y su continuidad a la fecha.

title: JICA COVID-19 Webinar #2 "Japan’s Public Health Approach for COVID-19 - past, present, and future-"
description:
JICA COVID-19 Webinar Series brings together leading health professionals from Japan to share Japan’s knowledge and experience on COVID-19 response and discuss the implications of their work. This is the 2nd webinar and we will invite Prof. Hitoshi Oshitani as a speaker. Prof. Hitoshi Oshitani; MD, MPH, PhD, is a Professor at Department of Virology, Tohoku University Graduate School of Medicine, Japan; a member of the Subcommittee on Novel Coronavirus Disease Control under the Japanese government Advisory Council. Between 1999 and 2005 Prof. Oshitani was an Infectious Diseases Control Advisor at the WHO’s Regional Office for the Western Pacific, the Philippines, during which he coordinated the response to SARS. 

Webinar Structure
 - introduction (5min)
 - Presentation by Prof.Oshitani (40 min)
 - Q&A, discussion (40 min)
 - Closing (5 min)

description:
The water leakage rates in distribution networks are considerably high in developing countries. It can be the potential cause of water contamination, low water pressure and intermittent water supply. The aim of this program is to obtain and upgrade knowledge and technical skills on non-revenue water management. On 4th February, 12 participants joined the field work session, held in Training and Technical Development Center, Bureau of Waterworks, Tokyo Metropolitan Government. The participants first studied the Leakage Prevention and Waterworks Mapping System in Tokyo. Afterwards, they experienced the practical field work based on the lecture content.

title: A video message from Dr. Kitaoka, president of JICA to celebrate the initiation of "JICA Chair"
description:
JICA launched the "JICA Development Studies Program" in 2018 to provide future leaders of developing countries with opportunities to not only receive education and pursue research in Japan, but also to learn about Japan's modernization experience. As one part of this programme, JICA started "JICA Chair" to share our country's experience and knowledge with JICA partners especially targeting the top universities in developing countries. 

This video message is released by Shinichi Kitaoka, the president of JICA, for celebrating the initiation and the holding of innovative JICA Chair Program in the Latin America and the Caribbean region.

JICA's vision is "Leading the World with Trust." We believe forging trust between countries is more critical now than ever before. With trust at the core of our cooperation, JICA implements its programs with partner countries on the basis of mutual understanding and respect - not from an unequal footing characterized by “aid” or “assistance.”

title: JICA COVID-19 Webinar #6 "Response to COVID-19 by Public Health Centers in Japan"
description: JICA COVID-19 Webinar Series starting January 2021 brings together various leading health professionals from Japan to share Japan’s knowledge and experience on COVID-19 response and discuss the implications of their work. The webinar is intended primarily for health professionals in low- and middle-income countries. In this 6th webinar, we will invite two directors of Public Health Centers (“hokenjo” in Japanese) as guest speakers. Dr YOMO, Akihiro, Director, Fukui Prefectural Public health Center, will give an overview of public health system in Japan and the role of public health centers, as well as the COVID-19 response during pandemic In Japan. Dr TSURUGI, Yoko, Director, Kikuchi Prefectural Public Health Center, Kumamoto Prefecture, will present various cases of specific COVID-19 measures at public health centers. [Program] Opening Remarks & Introduction of Speakers MAKIMOTO, Saeda, JICA Ogata Research Institute for Peace and Development Presentation by Dr YOMO, Akihiro “Japanese local health system and roles of public health centers” Presentation by Dr TSURUGI, Yoko “PHC and specific cases of Covid-19 in Japan” Q&A

title: Webinar on Changing Landscape of Development Cooperation in Southeast Asia
description: In this webinar, we would shed light on the realities of development cooperation in Southeast Asian region with an emphasis on the analysis of South-South Cooperation (SSC) by the “emerging donors” in the region. Specifically, Thailand’s endeavor to be a more active regional provider of development cooperation, Indonesia’s recent move to establish its streamlined aid agency (Indonesian AID), and Vietnam’s emergence as a provider of SSC to neighboring states, are discussed.

title: JICA COVID-19 Webinar #5 "How Ag-RDTs will change the course of COVID-19 pandemic"
description: In the 5th JICA COVID-19 Webinar, we focused on the role and effective use of antigen-detecting rapid diagnostic tests (Ag-RDTs) for COVID-19. We invited Prof. YANAGIHARA Katsunori, MD.,Ph.D, Nagasaki University Graduate School of Biomedical Sciences in Japan, as a keynote speaker to present experience in the use of Ag-RDTs in Japan. Afterward, as an introduction to the Ag-RDTs approved in Japan, Mr. Oi of FUJIFILM Corporation introduced an antigen test kit that uses silver amplification technology. Program: -Housekeeping & Opening Remarks (10min) -“The role and effective use of Ag-RDTs for COVID-19 and experience in the use of Ag-RDTs in Japan” (20min) Presentation by Prof. YANAGIHARA Katsunori -“Japanese technology and approved Ag-RDTs FUJIFILM COVID-19 Ag Test” (10min) Presentation by OI Koji -“Collaborative Effort of JICA and LMICs on COVID-19 testing” (5min) Presentation by Dr. ISONO Mitsuo -Q&A Session (30min)

title: Knowledge Forum 'Tackling Extreme Climate Events Around the World'
description: Efforts to address climate change continue to accelerate regardless of the COVID-19 pandemic. During the plenary meetings of the UN General Assembly in September 2020, many states made announcements on their roadmaps to reduce carbon dioxide emission and to achieve carbon neutrality. Moreover, extreme climate events such as torrential rain, floods and heatwaves are frequently occurring around the world, and it has been reported that global warming is one major cause of these. Under such circumstances, measures for climate change adaptation are increasingly seen to be important, along with those for climate change mitigation that aim to reduce carbon dioxide emission. Meanwhile, many challenges remain in identifying what programs could lead to adaptation. Currently, efforts are moving forward by further developing existing programs. In this forum, Mimura Nobuo, distinguished fellow at the JICA Ogata Sadako Research Institute for Peace and Development (JICA Ogata Research Institute) and specially appointed professor at the Global and Local Environment Co-creation Institute of Ibaraki University, gave a keynote speech about domestic and international trends in current efforts for climate change adaptation. The content of the Sixth Assessment Report (AR6 by the IPCC Working Group II), which is to be published in 2022, and discussions that took place in COP26 will be covered as well. Mimura also made recommendations for Japan’s roles in global collaboration. Furthermore, based on this keynote speech, we invited Mimura and Narita Daiju, visiting fellow at JICA Ogata Research Institute and associate professor at the University of Tokyo, to a panel talk session. While taking questions from the audience, opinions on future efforts for climate adaptation were extensively exchanged, with an aim to collect some suggestions on global collaboration in the future.
